name: Antietam
label: Homestead
lede: Two Louisville punk pioneers moved to New York, put out records for forty years, and never once sounded like the same band twice in a row.

eras.title: Louisville, then a one-way ticket
eras.text: Tara Key and Tim Harris came out of the first wave of Louisville punk, then moved to New York and started over as a trio with a name borrowed from the bloodiest day of the Civil War.

q: a kind of magical spontaneous combustion
yt: Tara Key on WRFL-FM's Trivial Thursdays
years.h: Louisville punk starts in living rooms and barns
years.p: Tara Key plays in No Fun and Tim Harris co-founds the Babylon Dance Band, two of the first bands in a scene that appears within weeks in 1978.
years.xp:
Harris told LEO Weekly the scene arrived as "a kind of magical spontaneous combustion" in 1978, with No Fun, Babylon Dance Band, the Endtables, the Blinders and the I-Holes all forming around the same time. They played barns, galleries and living rooms before the South 40 in Iroquois gave them a room.

Key joined Babylon Dance Band after Harris started it. Chronogram dates the band 1978 to 1983.

years.h: Key and Harris leave Kentucky for New York
years.p: Perfect Sound Forever dates the move to fall 1983, months before the band that became Antietam had a name.
years.xp:
Key told Perfect Sound Forever that landing on the cover of the Village Voice within the first year and a half of "having a band" (with Babylon Dance Band) made it easier to "grab the bullhorn."

Sources place them in Hoboken, near Maxwell's, in these years. AllMusic instead says the move came in the late 1980s, which the other accounts contradict.

years.h: Derby Day 1984: Antietam is born, named for a battle
years.p: Key and Harris start the band with Wolf Knapp and Michael Weinert. The name comes from the Civil War's bloodiest day.
years.xp:
LEO Weekly puts the founding on Derby Day 1984. Chronogram reports that D. Boon of the Minutemen ribbed them for using the Northern name for the battle when the Southern one, Sharpsburg, was right there.

Wikipedia and Rock and Roll Globe both list Knapp and Weinert in the first lineup; Knapp left after the early recordings.

eras.title: Homestead takes them on
eras.text: Two records for Gerard Cosloy's Homestead label put the band on the New York and college-radio map, even if Key's guitar was still hiding in the mix.

years.src: The Noise Room · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Antietam (band)
years.p: Gerard Cosloy signs the band after seeing them open for Hüsker Dü at Maxwell's in Hoboken, according to The Noise Room.
years.xp:
The Noise Room says the band's first show was at CBGB and that Cosloy found them at Maxwell's. Trouser Press was lukewarm about the first two records, calling the songs "a bit too inconspicuous, too gentle" and saying Key's guitar was not yet fully on display.

Wikipedia dates the release to July 1985.

years.h: Music from Elba: Sean Mulhall on drums, one time only
years.p: Mulhall, formerly of Babylon Dance Band, drums on this second Homestead album and nowhere else in the Antietam catalog.
years.xp: A "Until Now / Rain" single also came out on Homestead in 1986. Then the band went quiet for about three years.

eras.title: Yo La Tengo, CBGB and a new drummer
eras.text: A move to Triple X, two Yo La Tengo producers and a 20-year-old drummer turned a polite indie band into a loud one.

years.h: Burgoo: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley run the board
years.p: The Yo La Tengo couple produce the first Triple X album, with Charles Schultz on drums.
years.xp: A 1989 single, "Eaten Up by Hate" with "Naples" and "Day Before Tomorrow," on Triple X came first. Trouser Press calls Burgoo the point where Key's angular guitar comes forward.

years.src: Rock and Roll Globe · Wikipedia: Antietam (band)
years.h: Josh Madell, age 20, takes the drum stool
years.p: Josh Madell replaces Charles Schultz and is still the band's drummer 34 years later.
years.xp: Rock and Roll Globe says Madell was 20 when he joined. It names Mike Weinert as the outgoing drummer, while Wikipedia names Schultz; see questions.

years.h: Everywhere Outside: Madell arrives and the volume goes up
years.p: Trouser Press hears the intensity jump on the first album with Madell.

years.h: Antietam Comes Alive!: a live album from CBGB
years.p: Recorded at the Bowery club and released on Triple X.
years.xp: Trouser Press describes it as hitting "with the room-spinning displacement of a furious tequila buzz" and calls it the group's most visceral document.

years.h: Rope-a-Dope: back to Homestead, with an 11-minute closer
years.p: Produced by Lyle Hysen and the band; Kaplan plays on "Hands Down" and the band covers Dead Moon's "Graveyard."
years.xp:
AllMusic called it "an unjustly overlooked piece of mid-'90s indie rock," and Guitar Player praised Key's distorted tone. "Silver Solace" runs 11 minutes.

The same year Key released her solo album Bourbon County on Homestead, followed by Ear and Echo in 1995.

years.h: Key plays the Factory house band in I Shot Andy Warhol
years.p: Tara Key appears with Yo La Tengo as the band in the 1996 film; the Antietam single "Alibi" comes out on Other Music the same year.
years.xp: Members kept busy in between: Key made Dark Edson Tiger (1999, Thrill Jockey) with Rick Rizzo of Eleventh Dream Day, Harris played with Yo La Tengo, and Madell drummed in Codeine and Retsin.

eras.title: Carrot Top and their own label
eras.text: After roughly a decade away from albums, the band returned on Chicago's Carrot Top, then started its own imprint.

years.h: Victory Park: first album in ten years, on Carrot Top
years.p: The reunion record is the first of three for the Chicago label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Opus Mixtum · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Opus Mixtum: two discs, Rick Rizzo on guitar
years.p: Recorded at Seaside Lounge with Josh Clark; one track is a cover of the Rugbys.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band first imagined an instrumental-only record. Tenth Life followed in 2011, their third for Carrot Top; AllMusic and PSF describe it as poppier.

years.h: Intimations of Immortality on their own Motorific Sounds
years.p: The band releases the album on its own label.

eras.title: Forty years in
eras.text: Four decades on, the trio is still making records, with a second generation joining in.

years.h: Forty years in: Pitch & Yaw, a four-song EP
years.p: LEO Weekly says the band called it some of their strongest material.
years.xp: Madell's daughter Trixie performed with the band during Yo La Tengo's 2024 Hanukkah shows, per Magnet.

years.src: Chronogram · Magnet · Into Music · Listen Local
years.h: The Counting Game: album fourteen, on Dromedary
years.p: Released the same weekend the band plays Dromfest in Catskill, New York (September 4-6).
years.xp: The album includes Trixie Madell on "Spy Vs. Spy" and banjo from Steve Cooley. The opener "Way Too Well" is a garage rocker from 1997 that had never been released.
